data.gender_notes: Satyabhama is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: One who has truth as her wealth; Wife of Lord Krishna. The name Satyabhama carries the meaning “Truthful Lady” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Satyabhama usually hope their child will grow to embody truthful lady and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: The name Satyabhama holds significant cultural importance in Hindu mythology. Satyabhama, one of the wives of Lord Krishna, is depicted as being dutiful, virtuous, and truthful. She is known for her unwavering devotion and loyalty to her husband. In various Hindu texts and folklore, she is often portrayed as a strong and fearless queen, who uses her wisdom and intelligence to protect her people and uphold the principles of dharma.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Satyabhama embodies the spiritual values of truth, integrity, and loyalty. It emphasizes the importance of leading a life that is grounded in truthfulness and honesty. In Hindu spiritual traditions, it is believed that by invoking the name of Satyabhama, one can invoke the blessings of the Goddess of Truth, who bestows upon her devotees the inner strength and courage to speak the truth and live an authentic life. It also symbolizes the spiritual ideal of a harmonious marriage, where both partners are devoted to each other and uphold the values of truthfulness and loyalty.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Satyabhama, meaning 'truthful as the god Vishnu's consort', embodies the virtues of truth, devotion, and strength. In Hindu mythology, she is an embodiment of the unwavering support and unyielding love a wife should offer her husband.

vedic_reference.note: Not found in Vedas or Upanishads.

modern_usage.modern_context: In today's interconnected world, the name Satyabhama continues to be cherished by Hindu families globally. It is frequently featured on social media platforms where parents share their naming journeys, and Hindu name websites where expectant parents research meaningful names. The name bridges traditional Hindu values with modern Indian identity, making it relevant for contemporary families seeking names with deep spiritual and cultural significance.
